contents.text:
status reports the current or last run over the project's KB, detached or in
the foreground, of either kind — a build or a score run, whichever is newest.

For a build, "state" is none, running, cancelled, interrupted, failed, bounded
or finished; none means no build stands: kb-root/ is absent, or was removed
with no build since. "state-dir", "pid", "started", "updated", "ended" and
"no-inference" name the run and its timing. "stages" marks each stage done or
not done, and "current" gives the current stage's "stage", "units-done" and
"units-total"; each completed stage's commit, with the command that rewinds to
it, is in `build-trail {}`. "recent-refusals", "recent-fallbacks",
"cache-entries" and "cache-bytes", the last two the answer cache's size, are
the state store's history and outlive the build. "resume" is the call that
resumes the build.

For a score run, "state" is running, interrupted, done, cancelled, failed,
refused or retry. "state-dir", "pid", "started", "run" and "pass" name the run
and its timing. "counts", "scored" and "failures" give its progress. "resume"
is the call that resumes the run.

Arguments:
  `state-dir` (string): the run's state store (default: the store of the run holding the operation lock, else the KB's own store under $XDG_STATE_HOME/kbase)

build converts LaTeX volume roots — each a paper's top .tex file, never one
another includes — into a KB at kb-root/, in the git worktree root: one
tree, each volume its own directory, entry-point.md listing every volume in
path order. A volume root is the file 00README.json's toplevel entry names,
else the sole file containing \documentclass. A relative `volume-root` or
`bibliography` resolves against the project root, and the build orders each
list by full path, whatever order it was given in. With no `bibliography`,
every .bib beside any volume root is offered to every volume, in sorted order.
Where two nodes of one kind would share a title, the build suffixes the later
" (2)", " (3)" and so on: every title is unique within its kind, as every
write requires.

It walks the build's stages in order through the stage `through` names.
Each stage's boundary is a commit, its subject "kb-build: <stage> | <display>",
scoped to kb-root/, the build's records in kb-root/.build/ included; the
commit records the inputs, and the start boundary also records started-at, the
commit the build began from. The trail is the kb-build: commits on the current branch.

A fresh build takes volume roots and is refused where kb-root/ exists in any
state, a skeleton-only one and one an interrupted build left included.
`resume` takes no volume roots and no `bibliography`, and continues the trail with
the inputs it records. It is refused where kb-root/ does not exist (run a
fresh build) and where kb-root/ stands with nothing to resume; removing
kb-root/ is how to start over: kbase does not inspect half-built state. `build-trail {}` lists each
boundary's commit with the command that rewinds to it — a reset, then a resume
— and started-at's, the reset alone. A finished `no-inference` build never
runs its dropped steps — a step is a part of a stage's work — and a resume
over it changes nothing: to build with inference, run started-at's command
from `build-trail {}`, then a fresh build.

`no-inference` drops each step that would spend inference; every stage
is still walked and committed. Without it, the claim graph's multichoice
asks go to the endpoint [models] decision names and the overview passage to
the one [models] text names — each value a provider/model reference, the
provider that supplies the endpoint then the model it serves — and a build
missing either is refused.

Build state lives in `state-dir`, by default the KB's own store under $XDG_STATE_HOME/kbase.
One repository carries one run at a time, a build or a score run: a second is
refused, naming the holder's verb and pid. A run's own result names each stage
walked, its boundary commit and its report, and the call that resumes the
build where it did not finish.

Arguments:
  `volume-root` (list of string): each paper's top .tex file, a relative path resolving against the project root; required unless `resume`, refused with it
  `ask-concurrency` (integer): model calls in flight at once, across every role; at least 1 (default: [asks] concurrency in config.toml, else 4)
  `bibliography` (list of string): a .bib citations resolve against, one per file, read in path order (default: every .bib beside any volume root, sorted)
  `no-inference` (boolean): skip each step that would spend inference; every stage is still walked
  `resume` (boolean): continue the build the commit trail records, with the inputs it records
  `state-dir` (string): the run's state store (default: the KB's own store under $XDG_STATE_HOME/kbase)
  `through` (string): the last stage to walk, by id — start, document-graph, spine-seed, claims-declared, claims-discovered, equations-minted, references-found, claims-culled, depends-attributed, analyses-split, phase-3a or overview-drafted — or by display name (default: every stage)

The call returns once the run has started, as a detached process that carries
on without the server. Its result gives "pid", "state-dir" and "wait", a shell
command line that blocks until the run ends; no tool waits. The status tool
follows the run and the cancel tool stops it.

find lists the nodes matching every filter given, across every kind; with no
filter it lists every node. find locates nodes; show reads one. Each row is the
node's id, node_type, title, label (a work's citation key or an axiom's label;
null for a claim, an analysis or an experiment), host (the leaf stating it; null
for a work, an axiom or a node with no statement marker), strength and
dependents (the count of nodes its strength enters). A claim's or an
analysis's strength is derived; a work's, an experiment's or an axiom's is its
rigor.

`kind` repeats, keeping the nodes of any kind it names. `label`
matches only works and axioms, the kinds that carry a label. `path` matches
a node's host, so a node whose host is null never matches it. `min` and `max`
compare scored strengths only: a pending node matches neither, so `min: 0`
keeps exactly the scored nodes, and `sort: strength` without it ranks the
pending ones first. `pending` is refused beside `min` or `max`.

Sort ties break by ascending strength, then ascending id, in either `order`.

Arguments:
  `kind` (list of string): only nodes of this kind, one of claim, analysis, experiment, axiom, work
  `label` (string): only works and axioms whose label contains this, case-insensitively
  `limit` (integer): only beside an explicit `sort` and never 0: keep the first N of its order, or the last N for a negative N
  `max` (number): only nodes scored strictly below this
  `min` (number): only nodes scored at or above this
  `min-dependents` (integer): only nodes with at least this many dependents
  `order` (string): the sort's order: ascending or descending (default: ascending)
  `path` (string): only nodes whose host is this leaf or lies under this kb-root-relative directory, "" or . for kb-root; never a node with a null host
  `pending` (boolean): only nodes with no strength yet
  `sort` (string): the key to sort by: id, strength, dependents (default: id)
  `title` (string): only nodes whose title contains this, case-insensitively
